subject: Acme: control-plane exposure decomposition & mitigation map
messages:
From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@acme.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@acme.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: control plane exposure details for Dedicated & Private

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Acme's audit team asked for a focused deliverable: a single-page decomposition that shows where Redwood's control plane can reach or be reached by customer workloads for both Dedicated and Private deployments, and the mitigations you apply at each boundary. They want this scoped to: routing/egress points, KMS interactions, and any control-plane telemetry egress.

Can you provide a short "exposure + mitigation map" and a checklist of artifacts we can attach to the SOC 2/SIG submission? Ideally a diagram + one-page narrative + a CSV listing egress hosts/services.

We are aiming to include this in our SIG questionnaire next Friday (2026-10-01). Is that feasible?

Best,
Elaine Turner
Senior Security Engineer
Acme Corp

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control plane exposure details for Dedicated & Private

Thanks, Elaine — we can do that.

Scope confirmation:
- Focus: control-plane (API control signals, orchestration, health-checks) and the minimal set of telemetry/metrics/logs Redwood ships off-cluster.
- Exclude: in-band customer inference payloads and tokens (those are handled per-customer tenancy and are not part of the control-plane exposure doc).

Planned deliverables:
1) "Exposure decomposition" diagram (PDF) that marks ingress/egress interfaces for Dedicated and Private deployments.
2) One-page narrative summarizing each boundary, risk, and mitigation (network ACLs, mutual TLS, KMS policies, least-privilege service accounts).
3) CSV enumerating resolved egress targets (FQDNs/IPs), ports, and purpose.

Target: share draft by Mon 2026-09-27 EOD PT so you have a day to review before your SIG submission.

Kimberly / Jordan — can you confirm KMS and telemetry notes below so I can include the details in the narrative?

Thanks,
Mateo
Security Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control plane exposure details for Dedicated & Private

Quick notes for the narrative — save as bullet-friendly items:

- KMS boundary: Customer keys (Private) stay in customer-managed KMS (BYOK) when requested; Redwood only receives wrapped keys and performs operations in a short-lived HSM-backed session. For Dedicated, keys are stored in a Redwood-managed tenant KMS but are isolated per-reservation with strict IAM policies.
- Key material never traverses public internet in plaintext; wrapping/unwrapping uses mTLS + HC policies.
- Control-plane API endpoints are in a separate management VPC with no inbound rDNS for customer workloads; we peer via dedicated interconnects or VPC peering where required.
- Telemetry: aggregated metrics are pushed to a telemetry sink; raw logs that may contain minimal operational identifiers are redacted before egress. Retention windows configurable per-customer.

I'll attach a short note file with the KMS policy references.

-kim
Lead, Platform Security

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control plane exposure details for Dedicated & Private

Adding network specifics for the CSV:

- Dedicated: control-plane egress limited to: registry.redwood-inference.internal (443), kms.redwood-inference.internal (443), telemetry-sink.redwood-inference.internal (9443). All over private interconnect; source CIDRs are the Reserved GPU pool subnets.
- Private (VPC): control-plane can be routed through the customer's transit gateway or our region-specific relay. When routed through customer transit, egress targets are identical but may resolve to customer-provided endpoints (we document that mapping in the CSV).
- If air-gapped, we provide an "airlock" package with signed artifacts and an offline key ceremony; note that telemetry is optional and requires a documented acceptance checklist from the customer.

Also: I'll upload the preliminary diagram to the shared drive and link it in the deliverable.

-jb
Principal Infra Engineer

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@acme.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: control plane exposure details for Dedicated & Private

Elaine — attaching the deliverables per the plan. See attached: controlplane_exposure_decomp_v1.pdf (diagram + legend), private-dedicated-egress-table.csv (egress targets, ports, purpose), kms-boundary-notes.txt (policy excerpts and references).

Summary highlights (one-liners you can paste into SIG response):
- Control-plane is logically isolated in a management VPC with explicit peering/relay attachments for Dedicated and Private.
- KMS interactions are wrapped; customer-managed keys are supported for Private (BYOK).
- Telemetry egress is limited, redacted, and configurable; default retention aligns with SOC 2 controls.
- Air-gapped/private-only installs are supported with an offline artifact package; telemetry is opt-in and documented in an acceptance checklist.

Next steps: Elaine, please confirm acceptance of these artifacts and call out any gaps. If you want, we can do a quick 30-minute review on Wed (09/29) to walk through the diagram before your SIG submission.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Security Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: controlplane_exposure_decomp_v1.pdf (diagram), private-dedicated-egress-table.csv (CSV), kms-boundary-notes.txt (text)
